title: Ontology Enrichment for Effective Fine-grained Entity Typing

problem.claim: Zero-shot fine-grained entity typing must identify specific entity types from contextual information when only an ontology is provided.

gap.claim: Existing ontology structures often lack rich supporting information and contain ambiguous relations, while language models may lack interaction with task-specific ontologies.

contributions.claim: The proposed method enriches ontology nodes with instance information for training-sample augmentation and topic information for relating types to contexts.
It uses a coarse-to-fine typing algorithm that trains an entailment model with contrasting topics and instance-based augmented training samples.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that øurs achieves high-quality fine-grained entity typing without human annotation.
The authors report that øurs outperforms existing zero-shot methods by a large margin and rivals supervised methods.
The authors report strong transferability to unseen and finer-grained types.

narrative_sequence.summary: Fine-grained entity typing identifies specific entity types for entity mentions using contextual information.
Human annotation is costly at scale, motivating weakly supervised and zero-shot approaches.
The study considers zero-shot typing with only an ontology, but existing ontologies and language models have limitations.
The method enriches ontology nodes and applies a coarse-to-fine entailment-based typing algorithm.
The authors report strong performance without human annotation, competitive results against supervised methods, and transferability to unseen and finer-grained types.
